To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TRPM4 and the TRPM5 channels are expressed in VP neurones and are involved in the generation fDAPs.

the fast depolarizing after potential (fDAP), which is involved in the generation and maintenance of phasic bursts of action potential firing, is mediated by the melastatin-related subfamily of TRP channels, TRPM 4 and TRPM 5, and that TRPM 5 is specifically expressed in VP cells, whereas TRPM 4 is expressed in both VP and OT cells.
TRPM5 is specifically located in VP neurons, and that it is likely that TRPM5 plays a role in the generation of phasic bursting in VP neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the generation of firing patterns in VP and OT neurone, which is essential for the regulation of the secretion of the neurohypophysial hormone.
the electrophysiological properties of VP neurone and the mechanisms of VP secretion.
the electrophysiological properties of magnocellular neurones in the rat hypothalamus, and with the mechanisms underlying the generation of the distinct firing patterns in these neurones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fDAP in VP neurones is likely to be generated by a TRPM5 current.
TRPM4 is involved in the generation and maintenance of the fDap in VP and OT neurone, and TRPM5 is specifically involved in the generation but not maintenance of the fDAp in VP neurones.
TRPM4 and 5 are expressed in both VP and OT neurons, but that TRPM5 is the more important of the two in determining the firing pattern of the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPM5 and TRPM4 are involved in the generation and modulation of the firing patterns of VP and OT neurone in the SON and PV respectively.
TRPM5 and TRPM4 may be involved in the regulation of the firing properties of VP and OT neurone in SON.
TRPM5 is a candidate channel for the generation of fDAPs and that TRPM4 and/or TRPM5 are responsible for the generation of DAPs and the firing patterns of magnocellular neurones.

TRPM5 is a specific marker for VP neurones.
the TRP channels are important in the regulation of firing in magnocellular neurones.
